children: The listing follows the acquisition by the Swiss-based, London-listed firm of
in a $2.6bn deal, which is due to complete at the end of this month. The secondary listing and start of trading on the JSE will take effect a few days before that, on 23 November.

Coca-Cola HBC, which was founded in Nigeria in 1951, announced just over a year ago it had agreed to buy a 75% stake in its African counterpart. The company currently serves around 760m consumers across 29 countries, but once the deal completes, it will become the world’s second-largest Coca-Cola bottling partner by beverage volume, serving around 1.2bn consumers.
It will also materially expand Coca-Cola HBC’s presence in Africa and create a "stronger platform for sustainable, profitable growth", the firm said.

To date, it has received merger control approvals of five of the six relevant jurisdictions. As a result, completion will go ahead but will not be implemented in Tanzania until the country’s Fair Competition Commission has given the tie up the green light.
Coca-Cola will continue to trade on the main markets of both the London Stock Exchanges and Euronext Athens following competition.
